name: Memory & Index
description: See and edit what Webbee remembers about your code — the code index (files, languages, symbols, commit) and the durable notes distilled while coding, with a plain explanation of where each piece is stored and when it updates.

tools.name: list_repos
tools.description: List every repository Webbee holds memory for — code index size, languages, how many durable notes, and how fresh each one is. Works on every surface (panel, Telegram, terminal).

RepoRecord.description: One repository Webbee holds memory for, as summarised for the list.
RepoRecord.title: RepoRecord

tools.name: get_index
tools.description: Show the code index for ONE repository: file and language breakdown, how many functions/classes are indexed, key symbols with file:line, semantic-search status, and the exact commit the index was built at.

repo.description: Which repo — its repo_key, or any fragment of its path/name. Empty = the most recently touched one.
repo.title: Repo

return_schema.description: The full structural map of ONE repo, exactly as the kernel stored it.
return_schema.title: RepoIndexRecord

tools.name: list_notes
tools.description: Show the durable notes Webbee has learned about a repository — the cloud-side WEBBEE.md: conventions, gotchas, where things live. Each note carries a position number for editing and when it was written.

repo.description: Which repo — its repo_key, or any fragment of its path/name. Empty = the most recently touched one.
repo.title: Repo

NoteRecord.description: One durable note about a repo — editable by its owner.
NoteRecord.title: NoteRecord

tools.name: explain_memory
tools.description: Explain exactly where Webbee's memory about your code is stored, what each store holds, who writes it and when it updates — with live counts from your own account.

return_schema.description: Where each piece of repo memory lives and when it updates — live numbers.
return_schema.title: MemoryExplainerRecord

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Teach Webbee a durable fact about a repository — it is remembered across machines and surfaces, and used on later coding turns.

repo.description: Which repo — repo_key or path fragment. Empty = most recent.
repo.title: Repo

citations.description: Optional file paths this fact is about, e.g. ['app/billing/service.py']
citations.title: Citations

return_schema.description:
Outcome of ONE note write (add / edit / delete).

Deliberately NOT ``NoteRecord``: a write does not return the stored entity,
it returns what CHANGED — the resulting text plus the displaced/removed
one and the surviving count. Typing it truthfully is what lets the narrator
and the audit ledger describe the mutation without re-reading the store
(federal V24).
return_schema.title: NoteOpRecord

tools.name: edit_note
tools.description: Correct one durable note by its position number (see list_notes) — the text is replaced and marked as edited by you.

position.description: Which note to change — its position number from list_notes (1-based)
position.title: Position

repo.description: Which repo — repo_key or path fragment. Empty = most recent.
repo.title: Repo

return_schema.description:
Outcome of ONE note write (add / edit / delete).

Deliberately NOT ``NoteRecord``: a write does not return the stored entity,
it returns what CHANGED — the resulting text plus the displaced/removed
one and the surviving count. Typing it truthfully is what lets the narrator
and the audit ledger describe the mutation without re-reading the store
(federal V24).
return_schema.title: NoteOpRecord

tools.name: delete_note
tools.description: Make Webbee forget one durable note by its position number (see list_notes). The note text is echoed back so nothing vanishes silently.

position.description: Which note to forget — its position number from list_notes (1-based)
position.title: Position

repo.description: Which repo — repo_key or path fragment. Empty = most recent.
repo.title: Repo

return_schema.description:
Outcome of ONE note write (add / edit / delete).

Deliberately NOT ``NoteRecord``: a write does not return the stored entity,
it returns what CHANGED — the resulting text plus the displaced/removed
one and the surviving count. Typing it truthfully is what lets the narrator
and the audit ledger describe the mutation without re-reading the store
(federal V24).
return_schema.title: NoteOpRecord

tools.name: delete_repo
tools.description: Permanently erase EVERYTHING Webbee remembers about one repository — its code index AND all its durable notes — from storage, and verify afterwards that no key survived. This cannot be undone: the notes are gone for good, while the code index only comes back if that repo is opened in the Webbee terminal agent again.

repo.description: Which repo to erase — its repo_key, or a fragment of its path/name. Required: erasing whatever happens to be most recent would be a coin flip with the user's memory.
repo.title: Repo

return_schema.description:
Outcome of erasing ONE repo's memory — a verified fact, not an intent.

``verified`` is the result of a fresh keyspace scan performed AFTER the
delete, and ``leftover_keys`` names anything that survived it. They are
modelled as first-class fields precisely so the answer cannot claim a
clean wipe while something remains: if the re-scan finds a key, the
record says so and the narrator has to report it.
return_schema.title: PurgeRecord

include_repo_memory.description: Include repository notes and code index in search.
include_repo_memory.title: Include Repo Memory
